correctness.rationale: For s=(a,b)≠0 with n=a²−db², write the two conic points as s/2±t(db,a); these are exactly the candidates on the orthogonal line. The resulting square equation is t²=(n−4)/(4dn); the nonsquare d produces the minus sign in 1−χ(n(n−4)). At the origin the count is q+1. The C+L fiber has 1−χ(a(a−2)) choices, and L+L covers just a=2. Thus when χ(a(a−2))≠1 a mixed representation already exists; on the remaining fibers neither line term nor the intersection correction can contribute. The identity for a quadratic with two distinct roots gives |A|=(q−3)/2. On a regular a∈A the quartic is squarefree and has square leading coefficient, so its smooth genus-one model has two rational points at infinity and B_a=−1−t_a; anisotropy and a≠±2 give Z_a≤2. At a=−2 the double root is removed explicitly: summing χ(−d)χ(4−db²) over b≠0 gives B_a=−1+χ(−1) and Z_a=1. These facts justify the estimate and the regular-fiber positivity bound (q−3−2√q)/2>0 for q≥11. Independent enumeration over the four smaller fields, including coefficient arithmetic for F₉, reproduced M₃,M₅,M₇,M₉=0,0,4,12 and the stated fibers. Changing nonsquare d rescales b, and affine equivalence follows by centering the anisotropic quadratic form, norm rescaling, and moving the tangent point by a norm-one multiplier. The unitary Fourier identity uses the factor q for this group of size q².
residual_risks: Exhaustive independent enumeration was limited to the fields needed for the threshold proof; the large-field assertion is supported by the character-sum and Hasse argument, not an extrapolation.
